messages:
sachin: Quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel switch we saw a regression in prefix caching. Baseline (pre-switch) prefix hit-rate across top-1k prefixes was ~62%. Post-switch it's ~47%. p50 gen latency +18ms, p95 +60ms, and token cost per 1k reqs up ~12% :rotating_light:

maria: Ugh. Any flamegraphs / perf traces we can look at?

sachin: Uploading the traces now. Main observation: the kernel change altered how KV keys are normalized for some tokenizers, causing mismatch in our prefix fingerprint. Flame: https://internal.prod/graphs/prefix-flame-3105.png

aj: Can we mitigate with a quick deploy-time prefill tonight? Small synthetic prefill hitting top prefixes would likely restore hit-rate while we fix the keying. Low-risk if we throttle and limit to 2x/sec per prefix. @sachin can you give a sample job?

sachin: Yes. Proposed plan = run targeted prefill for top-200 prefixes for the affected models (gpt-like and small-chat). Keep RPS low and stop on any errors. Example prefill job we can add to orchestration (crontab-style):

```yaml
name: prefill-top200
schedule: "0 3 * * *"  # 03:00 UTC daily (low traffic)
payload_source: s3://prod/prefill-lists/top200-{{model}}.json
rate_limit: 200r/m
per_prefix_rate: 2/s
modes: [deploy-time, scheduled]
stop_on_error: true
tags: [prefill, canary, kernel-3105]
```

And a simple probe curl to exercise the runtime prefill endpoint:

```bash
curl -X POST https://internal.api/prefill \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PREFILL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-13b", "prefixes":["How do I", "Summarize", "Write a short"], "options":{"max_tokens":8}}'
```

ops-bot: Scheduled job created: prefill-top200 (id=job-3105-prefill). Next run 3105006000 UTC.

kevin: How does this interact with autoscaler events? If nodes spin up during the run we'll miss seeding new KV partitions. Can we hook prefill into post-scale lifecycle so new machines get primed as they join?

taylor: We should avoid blanket seeding on every scale-up. Suggest: per-node on-join seed only the top-N prefixes that historically map to that shard (use local heatmap). That reduces synthetic traffic a lot. Also use per-model priming profiles so small models don't get seeded with big-chat prefixes.

maria: If the canary fix (KV key normalization tweak) doesn't land quickly, we should consider rolling kernel back to previous version for the affected fleets. Prefill is short-term band-aid but will cost tokens. Need cost guardrails.

sachin: Agreed. Short-term triage plan I can own: 1) run the scheduled prefill tonight limited to top-200, 2) spin a canary runtime with adjusted KV-key hashing (hash-v2) and validate hit-rate by 6h, 3) add a post-scale hook to the autoscaler to run a per-node priming job for the node's shard. I'll open the PR for the kernel tweak and the autoscaler hook.

Example quick synthetic load command to run manually for verification: 

```bash
# run a small targeted prefill for verification
python infra/scripts/run_prefill.py --model redwood-13b --prefix-file /tmp/top50.json --rate 150/m --max-tokens 8 --auth-token $PREFILL_TOKEN
```

aj: Sounds good. Please post the canary metrics when available. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Job job-3105-prefill started at 3105006000 UTC (targeting redwood-13b & redwood-chat-small).

ops-bot: Job job-3105-prefill finished at 3105007400 UTC. Result: seeded 120/200 prefixes (partial due to ephemeral 429s), short-window hit-rate bump to 54% (10m after run). Cost estimate: ~0.9k tokens seeded per prefix total.

kevin: Good to see short-term bump. We still need longer-term fix and autoscaler integration.

maria: Also add a metric tag to measure prefill vs organic hits so we can discount seeding when evaluating quality.

sachin: Yep — I'll add a request header `X-Prefill-Run: job-3105-prefill` during seeding and wire it into metrics. Will update thread with PR links + canary results.

aj: Thanks everyone. Let's keep the prefill conservative until we confirm the kernel fix.

taylor: FYI, I'll add a note to the runtime runbook about per-node priming and the shard-heatmap approach.

maria: Ping me when the rollback PR is ready (if needed).

sachin: On it. Will report back tomorrow morning with canary numbers. :eyes:
